newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mobutu, in hospital, still plans return to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu, in hospital, still plans return to Zaire.

text.p: President Mobutu Sese Seko, able to eat and walk unaided in his hospital room, is still planning to return home to try to halt a relentless advance by Tutsi rebels, his son and spokesman said on Tuesday.

Mobutu Nzanga, seeking to deny reports his father was gravely ill after he was admitted to hospital in Monaco at the weekend, said the 66-year-old president was in "permanent contact" with his beleaguered government.
"As soon as he returns home he will actively work to contain the situation," Mobutu Nzanga said of the rebels who captured Zaire's third largest town, Kisangani, at the weekend.

He said Mobutu rejected all ideas of talks with rebel leader Laurent Kabila. "Kabila is in the pay of multinationals and is simply a cover to give a Zairean colour to an attack from abroad," Mobutu Nzanga said.

The president, in power for 32 years and widely accused of corruption, has spent most of his time at his luxury villa on the French Riviera since he underwent surgery for prostate cancer in Switzerland last August.

"The president is as well as he was when he (last) arrived on the Cote d'Azur" in February, Mobutu Nzanga said. "He will soon leave hospital... When he leaves we'll invite you to his villa where you can see him and take photographs."
He gave no dates and the president's entourage has often proved over-optimistic in the past.
A week ago, Mobutu Nzanga had said the president was aiming to return to Zaire last weekend. And another spoksesman said on Monday that Mobutu might leave hospital on Tuesday.
The newspaper Le Monde said Mobutu had suffered haemorrhages in his bladder linked to last year's surgery and required frequent blood transfusions.
"This means a specialised treatment which in practice cannot be carried out in his country." the daily quoted a member of Mobutu's medical team as saying.
The daily Liberation, meanwhile, said Mobutu had suffered heart problems linked to his weakness after the cancer and a recent bronchitis.
Mobutu Nzanga gave no details of the president's condition but said "he is walking and feeding himself normally".
Mobutu has two personal bodyguards in a room alongside his and two Monte Carlo policemen in the hospital's urology ward. He is cared for by his personal doctor, his wife and his son.
As wild rumours concerning Mobutu's health and a possible military coup circulated in Kinshasa, Kabila vowed on Tuesday to take over the country.
He promised a temporary ceasefire for 20 km (13 miles) around Kisangani to allow in humanitarian aid and let people who fled return, but said advances elsewhere would continue.
The French Foreign Ministry said on Monday that Mobutu's health was "a source of concern" in the clearest indication so far that his physical state was deteriorating along with his grip on power.
